title: Multicolor Quantum Dot Encoding for Polymeric Particle-Based Optical Ion Sensors

conflicts.ligand: Methods p.3 heading says TOPO-capped, body says capped with trioctylphosphine (TOP); Results p.4 and Figure1 caption say TOPO. The exact ligand inventory is unresolved; neither description replaces the other.
conflicts.polymer: Main abstract p.1 and Materials p.3 identify decyl methacrylate; Results p.4 calls the DMA unit dodecyl methacrylate. Retain poly(MMA-DMA) as source abbreviation with unresolved alkyl-chain identity.
conflicts.sensor: Methods p.3 QD sensors: ionophore19.4 mmol/kg, ETH2439 5.2 mmol/kg, NaTFPB8.8/14.1/18 mmol/kg. Initial Results p.6: ionophore19.2 and ETH2439 5.4 with NaTFPB8.8. Table1 footnote b p.7: ionophore19.1, ETH2439 5.5, NaTFPB9 mmol/kg. Results p.7 assigns Figure5/6 to14.1 mmol/kg NaTFPB, with8.8 mmol/kg used as apparent fitted concentration. Table recipe and figures are not silently equated.
conflicts.control: Methods p.3 QD-free control: ionophore19.2, NaTFPB8.9, ETH2439 5.4 mmol/kg. Results p.7 comparison says8.8 mmol/kg NaTFPB. Table1 footnote c says19.1,9,5.5 mmol/kg respectively. Preserve each source statement and unresolved batch equivalence.
conflicts.charge: Results p.7 equates1.9wt% QD1 to5.3mmol/kg ion exchanger and states an estimated positive charge of2.8umol/g QDs. Direct division using0.019kg QD per kg composite gives278.9umol/g; source statements conflict dimensionally and no corrected value replaces the reported2.8umol/g.
